title: Second Thoughts at the Water's Edge

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: With one foot in the trading canoe, a villager suddenly feels they do not want to go: get in the canoe, or wave the others off.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The canoe is loaded. Three others are already in it. They're going down the coast for a few days to trade baskets, and (name1) has been looking forward to it for weeks. Now, with one foot in the water, (he/she) has a sudden strong feeling that (he/she) doesn't want to go. No reason. Just a feeling.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) gets in. The feeling stays for the first hour and then fades somewhere along the coast. The trip is good. Nothing goes wrong. (He/she) never finds out what the feeling was. It might have been nothing. (He/she) is glad (he/she) went, and also not entirely sure (he/she) was right to.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Go without me," says (name1). The others are surprised, but they go. (name1) watches the canoe out of sight and then stands on the beach, feeling foolish and relieved at the same time. The trip goes fine without (him/her). (He/she) never finds out what the feeling was either. It's alright not to know.
